stem: A 41-year-old man shakes his head side-to-side to signal 'no'. The movement occurring at the joint between his first and second cervical vertebrae is provided by which of the following joint types?

options.label: A
options.misconception: A uniaxial flexion-extension joint is being assigned to head rotation.
options.explanation: Hinge joints (knee, elbow, ankle) allow flexion and extension, not rotation; shaking the head 'no' is rotation at a pivot.

options.label: B
options.misconception: A biaxial thumb joint is being assigned to the neck.
options.explanation: Saddle joints (first carpometacarpal joint of the thumb) are biaxial, allowing flexion/extension and abduction/adduction with circumduction.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; the atlantoaxial joint is the classic pivot joint.
options.explanation: The atlantoaxial pivot joint (between C1 and C2) provides side-to-side rotation of the head around a single axis.

options.label: D
options.misconception: A multiaxial joint is being assigned to a uniaxial movement.
options.explanation: Ball-and-socket joints are found only at the shoulder and hip, where they permit multiaxial movement including rotation; the C1-C2 joint is a pivot.

options.label: E
options.misconception: A biaxial wrist-type joint is being assigned to the neck.
options.explanation: Condyloid joints (radiocarpal joint of the wrist, knuckles) are biaxial; the atlantoaxial joint rotates around one axis as a pivot.

context: Learning objective: the six synovial joint types. Pivot (atlantoaxial C1-C2 — head rotation), hinge (knee/elbow/ankle — flexion/extension only), condyloid (wrist/knuckles) and saddle (thumb) — biaxial, plane (intertarsal/vertebral facets — gliding), ball-and-socket (shoulder/hip — multiaxial, widest range).
